title: Paper Towels 6-roll

drivers.name: Store closure (Monday)
drivers.evidence: Store closed Monday; historical daily sales show ~15% of weekly volume on Mondays; no prior closure data, so effect is estimated from structure and noise-adjusted uncertainty.

drivers.name: Price increase (4.5%)
drivers.evidence: Prior week at $10.32 saw 96 units (baseline 96.5); price increase of 4.5% with no promotion shows no lift; historical price elasticity suggests ~3% demand drop per 5% price rise, applied conservatively.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 96.5. The target week has no event but a price increase to $10.32 (+4.5%) and a Monday store closure. Price increases reduce demand; past data shows no promotion at this price, but a prior $10.32 week (2026-09-28) sold 96 units (vs baseline 96.5), suggesting minimal impact. However, the store closure removes one day of sales. Given the product's daily sales variability and the absence of a promotion, the closure likely reduces sales by ~15% (1/7 of week). The uplift model suggests no effect, but judgment overrides it due to the closure. Evidence is limited (one past closure, no similar price change), so shrink toward 1.0. Final adjustment: downside from closure, moderate confidence.

brief:
PRODUCT: Paper Towels 6-roll | category Household | Store #12 (Austin, TX)
TARGET WEEK: 2026-11-30 to 2026-12-06 (8 weeks after the last week with sales data)

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:
  events: none
  shelf price: 10.32 (+4.5% vs regular price 9.88)
  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 96.5 | 5%-95%: 62.4 - 234.3 | 10%-90%: 67.0 - 191.9

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
